title: Carnivore Macros Calculator 2026 | Hacé Cuentas
description: Calculate carnivore diet macros in lbs/oz: 70-80% fat, 20-30% protein, ~0% carbs. Strict carnivore vs nose-to-tail vs animal-based. Ribeye, liver, electrolytes.
intro: The **carnivore diet** is an elimination protocol built on animal products only — zero carbohydrate by design, with energy delivered almost entirely from animal fat and protein. In US clinical practice we see three main camps. **Strict carnivore** (Shawn Baker MD's playbook) sticks to ruminant meat, salt, and water — no dairy, no eggs, no plants. **Nose-to-tail carnivore** (the early Paul Saladino MD approach) layers in organ meats — liver, heart, kidney, bone marrow — to backfill the micronutrients muscle meat alone underdelivers. **Animal-based** (Saladino's 2022 update) keeps the nose-to-tail base but adds raw honey, fruit, and raw dairy, which technically exits strict carnivore but is what many of my long-term patients actually run. Typical macros land around **70–80% of calories from fat, 20–30% from protein, and 0–5% carbs** (trace glycogen and organ carbs only). Nutritional ketosis is automatic — blood ketones generally sit at 0.5–2.0 mmol/L within 7–14 days. This calculator gives you grams of protein and fat for any calorie target so you can dial in a ribeye-and-eggs plate without guessing.
keyTakeaway: Carnivore macros: **70–80% fat, 20–30% protein, ~0% carbs**. A 180-lb male at 2,500 kcal needs ~200g protein + ~180g fat (≈ 2.5 lb ribeye 80/20). Add 5g sodium, 1g potassium, 400mg magnesium daily.
useCases: **Autoimmune protocol carnivore** — Hashimoto's, RA, psoriasis, UC flares: 30-90 day strict elimination, ruminant + salt + water, reintroduce one food at a time to map triggers.

**Type 2 diabetes remission** — patients with A1c 7-10% running strict carnivore typically drop A1c 1.5-2.5 points in 90 days and deprescribe metformin under MD supervision (mirrors Virta-style outcomes).
**Athlete strict cut** — fighters and physique competitors using 8-12 week strict carnivore at ~14 kcal/lb to lean out while protecting LBM (high protein floor 1g/lb).
**Shawn Baker-style strength training** — 4,000+ kcal/day, 2.5-3 lb fatty ground beef + eggs + organs, training 5x/week, leveraging the carnivore satiety signal to avoid bulking-phase fat creep.
**Long-term metabolic health** — patients with severe IBS, SIBO, or oxalate overload using 6-12 month carnivore as a gut reset, then transitioning to animal-based with reintroduced honey and fruit.

example.title: Example: 180-lb male, 2,500 kcal carnivore day
steps: **Protein**: `2,500 × 0.28 / 4` ≈ **175 g** (≈ 1g per lb bodyweight, Phinney protein ceiling for ketosis).
**Fat**: `2,500 × 0.72 / 9` ≈ **200 g** (fills remaining calories — fat is the energy lever, not protein).
example.result: Practical plate: 2 lb (32 oz) ribeye + 4 eggs + 3 oz beef liver weekly + 5g sodium + electrolytes. Or 2 lb 80/20 ground beef ≈ 1,800 kcal — supplement with butter/tallow to close the 700 kcal gap. Water to thirst, never force-hydrate (dilutes sodium).

explanation:
## The macro math, in lbs and oz

A 180-lb moderately active male sits around a **2,500 kcal TDEE**. On carnivore that translates to roughly **2.5 lb of ribeye** (USDA ribeye runs ~1,000 kcal/lb at typical 80/20 fat-to-protein split by calories), giving you about **200 g protein and 180 g fat**. If you'd rather run **2 lb of 80/20 ground beef**, you land at ~1,800 kcal — short of TDEE by 700 kcal, which is the gap most beginners miss. You close it with **3-4 tbsp butter, tallow, or bone marrow** (~100 kcal/tbsp), or add fatty cuts like brisket point or short rib.

## Why the fat-to-protein ratio is the whole game

Phinney and Volek's work pins the ceiling for protein in nutritional ketosis at roughly **2 g per kg lean body mass** (~1 g/lb for most). Push protein higher and **gluconeogenesis** ramps — the liver converts excess amino acids to glucose, blood ketones drop, and the metabolic state most carnivore patients are chasing (stable energy, appetite suppression, mental clarity) softens. Fat is what fills the calorie envelope above that protein floor. Practically: **protein is a structural target, fat is the energy dial**. Hungry? Add fat. Losing weight too fast? Add fat. Strength stalling? Hold protein, push fat.

## Electrolytes — non-negotiable

Ketogenic diets dump sodium through the kidneys (insulin-mediated sodium retention drops). Target daily intake on strict carnivore:

- **Sodium: 5,000 mg** (≈ 2 tsp added salt on top of food)
- **Potassium: 1,000-3,500 mg** (ribeye supplies ~370 mg per 4 oz; supplement if cramping)
- **Magnesium: 400 mg** (glycinate or malate; meat is magnesium-poor)

Missing electrolytes is the #1 reason people quit in week 2 — headaches, cramps, brain fog, palpitations. None of it is the diet failing; it's a sodium gap.

## Why I push organ meats (nose-to-tail logic)

Muscle meat is incomplete. **100 g of beef liver** delivers ~800% RDA vitamin A (retinol — preformed, no conversion needed), ~600% B12, ~50% riboflavin, ~30% iron, plus choline, copper, and folate. A weekly **3-4 oz portion of liver** closes the micronutrient gap that muscle-meat-only strict carnivore leaves open. Heart adds CoQ10. Bone marrow adds glycine and collagen precursors. Patients who run nose-to-tail report fewer 90-day labs showing low ferritin, folate, or B12.

## The N=1 evidence base (and where it's thin)

We don't have RCTs. What we have: **Shawn Baker MD** (orthopedic surgeon, multiple masters rowing records on strict carnivore), **Mikhaila Peterson** (autoimmune arthritis and depression remission, well-documented), **Anthony Chaffee MD** (neurosurgical resident, 10+ years strict carnivore, athletic performance maintained), and the Lennerz Harvard 2021 survey of 2,029 carnivores reporting high satisfaction and metabolic improvements at 6-14 months. The honest position: **strong N=1 signal, weak population evidence**, which is why I run pre/post bloodwork on every patient.

## Risks I monitor in my US carnivore patients

- **LDL elevation** — about 30% of the population are **lean mass hyper-responders** (LMHR phenotype described by Norwitz et al., Curr Opin Endocrinol Diabetes Obes 2022). LDL-C can hit 200-400 mg/dL. Whether this translates to ASCVD risk in a low-insulin, low-triglyceride state is the open question. We run CAC scans at baseline and 12 months.
- **Oxalate dumping** — patients with prior high-oxalate diets (spinach, almonds, chocolate) often get joint pain, skin rashes, and kidney discomfort in month 1 as stored oxalates mobilize. Slow the transition; don't go cold turkey if you've been a spinach-smoothie person.
- **Fiber controversy** — gut microbiome shifts dramatically. Whether the reduction in fiber-fermenting bacteria is a problem or a feature depends on the patient (it's a feature for IBS/IBD/SIBO patients).
- **30 days vs long-term** — 30-day carnivore is a safe elimination trial for almost anyone. **Long-term carnivore (1+ year)** needs annual labs: CMP, lipid panel with apoB, fasting insulin, A1c, ferritin, B12, vitamin D, RBC magnesium, and a CAC scan if LDL stays elevated.

Run labs **before you start** and at **90 days**. No exceptions.

faq.q: Do I need vitamin C on the carnivore diet?
faq.a: **No supplemental vitamin C required on strict carnivore.** Fresh muscle meat contains 1-2 mg/100g and beef liver around 23 mg/100g — small numbers, but vitamin C requirements drop dramatically without dietary glucose competing for the same GLUT-1 transporters (Stone's competitive inhibition hypothesis). I've never seen scurvy in a compliant carnivore patient. Eat fresh (not aged) meat, include liver weekly, and you're covered.

faq.q: What about constipation with no fiber?
faq.a: **Most patients normalize within 4-6 weeks.** Stool volume drops because there's almost no undigested residue — that's not constipation, that's efficient absorption. Real constipation (straining, hard stool, infrequent BMs with discomfort) usually means **not enough fat** or **not enough salt**. Bump fat to 75-80% of calories and sodium to 5g/day. If it persists past 6 weeks, add magnesium citrate 400-600 mg at bedtime.

faq.q: Will the carnivore diet wreck my cholesterol?
faq.a: **LDL-C goes up in most patients, sometimes dramatically.** About 1 in 3 are 'lean mass hyper-responders' (Norwitz 2022) with LDL-C 200-400 mg/dL. What matters more in the metabolic context: **apoB** (particle count), **triglyceride/HDL ratio** (should be under 1.5), **fasting insulin**, **A1c**, and a **CAC scan** to image actual plaque. Don't make the call on LDL-C alone — get the full picture with a lipidologist who understands the LMHR phenotype.

faq.q: Should I eat liver every week?
faq.a: **Yes — 3 to 4 oz of beef liver once a week is my standard recommendation.** That single portion delivers ~800% RDA vitamin A, ~600% B12, ~30% iron, plus choline, copper, and folate. More than that risks **vitamin A toxicity** (chronic intake above ~10,000 IU/day retinol can be problematic), so don't go daily. If you hate liver, blend it into ground beef 1:4 — you won't taste it. Desiccated liver capsules work but are inferior to fresh.

faq.q: Is coffee allowed on strict carnivore?
faq.a: **Technically no — it's a plant.** Shawn Baker drops it. Saladino allows it in his animal-based protocol. My take with patients: if you're running a **30-day strict elimination for autoimmune triage**, cut coffee — caffeine and chlorogenic acids are common triggers and you need a clean baseline. If you're running **long-term carnivore for metabolic health**, black coffee (1-2 cups) is fine and the data on coffee's metabolic effects is favorable.

faq.q: Is the carnivore diet safe for women?
faq.a: **Yes, but the protein floor matters more.** Women on carnivore who undereat protein (going below 0.8 g/lb bodyweight) sometimes see cycle disruption, hair shedding, and thyroid downregulation — same pattern as undereating on any diet. Target **1 g protein per lb bodyweight** as a floor, prioritize fatty cuts over lean, don't run aggressive caloric deficits, and track cycle and basal temperature. Pregnant or breastfeeding patients should not run strict carnivore without OB input.

faq.q: How do I run a 30-day carnivore trial?
faq.a: **Standard protocol I use with patients:** Week 0: baseline labs (CMP, lipid panel with apoB, fasting insulin, A1c, ferritin, B12, vitamin D, hs-CRP). Days 1-7: ruminant meat, salt, water only — expect 'keto flu' (fatigue, headache, irritability — it's the sodium gap). Days 8-21: add eggs and fatty fish if tolerated; add 3-4 oz liver in week 2. Days 22-30: maintain. Day 31: repeat labs, log symptoms (energy, sleep, joint pain, brain fog, autoimmune markers). Reintroduce one food category at a time over the next 30 days to map triggers.

faq.q: What's the difference between strict carnivore, nose-to-tail, and animal-based?
faq.a: **Strict carnivore** (Shawn Baker): ruminant meat, salt, water. No eggs, no dairy, no organs required. Cleanest elimination protocol. **Nose-to-tail** (early Saladino): strict carnivore + organ meats (liver, heart, kidney, bone marrow) to backfill micronutrients. My preferred default. **Animal-based** (Saladino 2022): nose-to-tail + raw honey, fruit, raw dairy. Technically exits carnivore (carbs return), but it's what most long-term patients converge on and tolerate best metabolically once they're fat-adapted.
